observation.description: When a nested mutation inside an action refuses with SNAPBACK_AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED (an outsider driving runReminder; a guest driving sendNotification), the caller receives only SNAPBACK_HANDLER_FAILED — the platform auth code does not survive the action boundary. The denial itself holds (nothing was delivered or created), but the uniform-denial diagnostic property that every direct read/subscribe/write surface upholds is lost one hop into the action lane: a client cannot distinguish 'you are not allowed' from 'the handler crashed'. Related to the app-level refusal collapse already owned by 0137-a3-f3, but this leg collapses a PLATFORM code, not an app Error.
evidence: demos/improvement-sweep/arms/a4-snapback-web/evidence/scenario-evidence.json (A4-09 outsiderActionDenied and A4-10 guestDenied both SNAPBACK_HANDLER_FAILED; A4-03 negative matrices show the direct surfaces returning SNAPBACK_AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED)

competitorOutcome.description: Convex actions rethrow ConvexError from nested runMutation calls with the structured data intact, so an auth refusal keeps its identity through the action boundary.

mustNotRegress: Non-disclosing uniform denials on direct surfaces, and the rule that nested mutations inherit the action's server-resolved authority rather than accepting a replacement identity.
smallestCoherentFix: Propagate the platform diagnostic class (at minimum SNAPBACK_AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED) from a nested mutation failure through the action's structured error envelope, keeping message bytes uniform and non-disclosing.
acceptanceWitness: An unauthorized principal invoking an action whose nested mutation requireRole-refuses receives SNAPBACK_AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED (byte-uniform with the direct-mutation denial), and an unrelated handler crash still surfaces as SNAPBACK_HANDLER_FAILED.
